subject: the work itself: finished pieces, in use, at real scale
direction: one light per page; straight-on or 25° above for objects; crop to the work, never the screen bezel
texture: none, or grain ≤ 0.06 on the ground
stand_in: a drawn cover per project in the page's illustration style, with the alt text the real image will have; [NEEDS ASSET] per project
avoid: mockups of work that was never made; stock desks and laptops

subject: the team at work and the work on the wall, in the studio's own room
direction: available light, eye height, 35–50 mm; people mid-task, nobody looking at the lens
texture: none, or paper under printed-matter sections
stand_in: project covers drawn as ledger plates or contact sheets; the studio room drawn once
avoid: stock team photos; collage of logos as imagery

subject: the product alone, then in use, then in detail (making, material, scale)
direction: one window light camera-left, soft, no fill; same angle for every product in a set; graded to the ground colour
texture: linen or paper only where the product is photographed on it
stand_in: a drawn study of the actual object (shape, glaze, material) on the page's ground; real dimensions in the caption
avoid: lifestyle stock; 3D renders presented as photographs

subject: the product's own UI, shown as UI (live components or a device frame)
direction: real screens with real data from the product's domain; never a blurred dashboard
stand_in: the UI built as components with realistic rows and names; [NEEDS ASSET] for real screenshots
avoid: stock photos of people at laptops; abstract blobs as 'product'

subject: the rooms, the courtyard, the view, the table: the place as a guest finds it
direction: one time of day per set (late afternoon is common); eye height; doors and windows in frame for scale
texture: none, or paper on rate cards
stand_in: the actual architecture drawn (arches, courtyard, rooms) in the page's style, one per room
avoid: drone shots of somewhere else; empty-bed stock; HDR grades

subject: the dishes, the room in service, the kitchen and the people
direction: overhead or 45° for dishes, consistent across the menu; warm practical light for the room
stand_in: drawn dishes from the real menu, labelled with their real names and prices
avoid: stock food; glistening over-styled plates the kitchen doesn't serve

subject: the work in the field: places, people doing it, documents and evidence
direction: documentary, available light, people with consent and names; no posed hand-shaking
texture: halftone or paper for reports and evidence
stand_in: drawn survey plates, maps and charts of the real issue; [NEEDS ASSET] with consent notes
avoid: poverty imagery without consent or names; stock 'hands holding a seedling'

subject: the stage, the line-up, the place: type is often the image
direction: poster logic: one bold mark, the date large; photographs only of the real performers
texture: grain or halftone, still, on the poster surfaces
stand_in: type as image plus a drawn stage-light or venue mark; performer photos as [NEEDS ASSET]

subject: buildings in their context, plans and sections, materials close up
direction: straight verticals (shift lens or corrected), one time of day, people small for scale
texture: none; plans drawn on the ground
stand_in: line drawings of the real plans, sections and elevations
avoid: renders presented as built photographs; skies replaced in post

subject: the person's words, with one honest portrait if any
direction: a single portrait in available light, looking at the work or the reader, not at a phone
stand_in: no stand-in image; the text and type carry the page; [NEEDS ASSET] for the portrait

subject: the product, shot as an object to understand: front, profile, inside, in use
direction: studio light, one key, consistent across the set; turntable or exploded view where it explains
stand_in: a drawn or rendered study of the real product (marked as a render); frame sequence from a storyboard for Tier 5
avoid: renders of features the product doesn't have; lifestyle stock

subject: the subject being taught: diagrams, worked examples, the classroom or field
direction: diagram style per the page's style; labelled, never decorative; photos of real students only with consent
texture: paper or grid only where it is the material (a workbook, graph paper)
stand_in: drawn diagrams of real lesson content with real labels; [NEEDS ASSET] for classroom photos
avoid: stock graduation caps; cartoon mascots that teach nothing
